Que.q: Q1 : What is Angular Framework?
Que.a: Angular is a platform and framework for building single-page client applications using HTML and TypeScript. Angular is written in TypeScript. Angular is a TypeScript-based open-source front-end platform that makes it easy to build applications with in web/mobile/desktop. The major features of this framework such as declarative templates, dependency injection, end to end tooling, and many more other features are used to ease the development.

Que.q: Q2 : What are Single Page Applications (SPA)?
Que.a: An SPA (Single-page application) is a web app implementation that loads only a single web document, and then updates the body content of that single document via JavaScript APIs such as XMLHttpRequest and Fetch when different content is to be shown.

Que.q: Q6 : What are the advantages of using Angular over AngularJS?
Que.a: Angular is a typescript based free and open-source application design framework and platform for developers which comes with many advantages.

list.1: Angular is at least five times faster than AngularJS due to a much better algorithm for data binding and a component-based architecture.
list.2: The components of an Angular application are quite independent and self-sufficient, which makes them reusable and test friendly.
list.3: The independent components are easier to replace, maintain, and scale-up.
list.4: Angular applications can be rendered both on browsers and mobile devices.
list.5: Angular has inbuilt extensions for server-side rendering of applications. This enables developers to sync client and server sides of content, a huge plus for SEO.
list.6: Angular supports lazy loading, which makes the applications faster as only those components that are needed are loaded.
list.7: TypeScript's first approach of Angular makes for cleaner code, better navigation, and high-quality product.

Que.q: Q15 : What are lifecycle hooks available?
Que.a: Angular application goes through an entire set of processes or has a lifecycle right from its initiation to the end of the application. The representation of lifecycle in pictorial representation as follows.

list.ngOnChanges: When the value of a data bound property changes, then this method is called.
list.ngOnInit: This is called whenever the initialization of the directive/component after Angular first displays the data-bound properties happens.
list.ngDoCheck: This is for the detection and to act on changes that Angular can't or won't detect on its own.
list.ngAfterContentInit: This is called in response after Angular projects external content into the component's view.
list.ngAfterContentChecked: This is called in response after Angular checks the content projected into the component.
list.ngAfterViewInit: This is called in response after Angular initializes the component's views and child views.
list.ngAfterViewChecked: This is called in response after Angular checks the component's views and child views.
list.ngOnDestroy: This is the cleanup phase just before Angular destroys the directive/component.

Que.q: Q19 : What is the difference between *ngIf and hidden?
Que.a: There is actually a performance difference between them:

list.*ngIf: ngIf will comment out the data if the expression is false. This way the data are not even loaded, causing HTML to load faster.
list.[hidden]: [hidden] will load the data and mark them with the hidden HTML attribute. This way data are loaded even if they are not visible.

Que.a: So [hidden] is better used when we want the show/hide status to change frequently, for example on a button click event, so we do not have to load the data every time the button is clicked, just changing its hidden attribute would be enough.

Que.note: Note : The performance difference may not be visible with small data, only with larger objects.

Que.q: Q28 : What is the difference between pure and impure pipe?

list.Pure pipe: A pure pipe is only called when Angular detects a change in the value or the parameters passed to a pipe.
list.An impure pipe: An impure pipe is called for every change detection cycle no matter whether the value or parameter(s) changes.

Que.list_heading: This is relevant for changes that are not detected by Angular

list.1: when you pass an array or object that got the content changed (but is still the same instance)
list.2: when the pipe injects a service to get access to other values, Angular doesn't recognize if they have changed.

Que.a: In these cases you probably still want the pipe to be executed.

Que.note: Note : You should be aware that impure pipes are prone to be inefficient. For example when an array is passed into the pipe to filter, sort, ... then this work might be done every time change detection runs (which is quite often especially with the default ChangeDetectionStrategy setting) event though the array might not even have changed. Your pipe should try to recognize this and for example return cached results.

Que.a: During each navigation, the Router emits navigation events through the Router.events property allowing you to track the lifecycle of the route.The sequence of router events is as below,

list.RouteConfigLoadStart: Before the router lazy loads a route configuration.
list.RouteConfigLoadEnd: After a route has been lazy loaded.
list.RoutesRecognized: When the router parses the URL and the routes are recognized.
list.GuardsCheckStart: When the router begins the guards phase of routing.
list.ChildActivationStart: When the router begins activating a route's children.
list.ActivationStart: When the router begins activating a route.
list.GuardsCheckEnd: When the router finishes the guards phase of routing successfully.
list.ResolveStart: When the router begins the resolve phase of routing.
list.ResolveEnd: When the router finishes the resolve phase of routing successfully.
list.ActivationEnd: When the router finishes activating a route's children.
list.ChildActivationEnd: When the router finishes activating a route.
list.NavigationError: When navigation fails due to an unexpected error.

Que.q: Q48 : Do I need a Routing Module always?
Que.a: No, the Routing Module is a design choice. But it is recommended when the configuration is complex and includes specialized guard and resolver services.

Que.q: Q49 : What is the difference between Eager Loading, Lazy Loading, and Pre-Loading?

list.Eager Loading: Feature modules under Eager Loading would be loaded before the application starts. This is the default module-loading strategy./Eager Loading: used to load core modules and feature modules that are required to start the application.
list.Lazy Loading: Feature modules under Lazy Loading would be loaded on demand after the application starts. It helps to start application faster./all other modules could be lazily loaded on demand after the application started
list.Pre-Loading: Feature Modules under Pre-Loading would be loaded automatically after the application starts./Pre-Loading: used to load specific feature modules that are very likely to be used soon after the application started.

Que.q: Q50 : When to use Eager Loading, Lazy Loading, and Pre-Loading?

list.Eager Loading: Case 1 : Small size applications. In this case, it’s not expensive to load all modules before the application starts, and the application will be faster and more responsive to process requests. Case 2 : Core modules and feature modules that are required to start the application. These modules could contain components of the initial page, interceptors (for authentication, authorization, and error handling, etc.), error response components, top-level routing, and localization, etc. We just have to eagerly load these modules to make the application function properly despite the application size.
list.Lazy Loading: The scenario of applying Lazy Loading is relatively simple and straightforward. In a big-size web application, we can lazily load all other modules that are not required when the application starts.
list.Pre-Loading: Case 1 : Medium size application. In this scenario, we can make the application start faster since it will load all other modules later that are not required to run the application. And the application would be more responsive to process users’ requests than applying Lazy Loading strategy since the application will load all these modules after the application started. Case 2 : Some specific modules that users are very likely to use after the application started. In this scenario, we can pre-load these feature modules and still lazy load other modules.

Que.q: Q60 : What is View encapsulation?
Que.a: In Angular, a component's styles can be encapsulated within the component's host element so that they don't affect the rest of the application.
The Component's decorator provides the encapsulation option which can be used to control how the encapsulation is applied on a per component basis.

list.1: ViewEncapsulation.ShadowDom, Angular uses the browser's built-in Shadow DOM API to enclose the component's view inside a ShadowRoot (used as the component's host element) and apply the provided styles in an isolated manner.
list.2: ViewEncapsulation.Emulated, Angular modifies the component's CSS selectors so that they are only applied to the component's view and do not affect other elements in the application (emulating Shadow DOM behavior). For more details, see Inspecting generated CSS.
list.3: ViewEncapsulation.None, Angular does not apply any sort of view encapsulation meaning that any styles specified for the component are actually globally applied and can affect any HTML element present within the application. This mode is essentially the same as including the styles into the HTML itself.

Que.note: ViewEncapsulation.ShadowDom only works on browsers that have built-in support for the shadow DOM (see Can I use - Shadow DOM v1). Not all browsers support it, which is why the ViewEncapsulation.Emulated is the recommended and default mode.

Que.q: Q71 : What are different between of Subject, BehaviorSubject and ReplaySubject?

list.1: In case of Subject, Observers who are subscribed at a later date will not obtain the data values emitted prior to their subscription.

In ReplaySubject, Observers who are subscribed at a later point will receive all the old data values issued prior to their subscription. As it operates by using a buffer that holds the values emitted and re-emits (replaying) a sequence of old values once new Observers are subscribed.

BehaviorSubject functions similar to ReplaySubject but only re-issues the last emitted value (current value). So you're interested in the last / current value of the observer, if BehaviorSubject is useful.

Que.q: Q72 : When we use the switchMap, mergeMap and concatMap?

list.flatMap/mergeMap: creates an Observable immediately for any source item, all previous Observables are kept alive. Note flatMap is an alias for mergeMap and flatMap will be removed in RxJS 8.
list.concatMap: waits for the previous Observable to complete before creating the next one.
list.switchMap: for any source item, completes the previous Observable and immediately creates the next one.
list.exhaustMap: source items are ignored while the previous Observable is not completed.

Que.q: Q74 : What is the difference b/w Hot Observable  and Cold Observable?

list.Hot observable: A hot Observable will start emitting as soon as it's created, and as such the values it emits are produced outside of it. A hot Observable's emitted objects are shared between its subscribers - this is called multicasting. Because of this behavior, an observer may start observing the sequence somewhere in the middle of it.
list.Cold observable: A cold Observable waits until an observer subscribes to it to start emitting. Observables are lazy by default, meaning they only execute when an observer subscribes to it. This behavior allows an observer to observe the entire sequence of emitted values.

Que.note: Note: When the data is produced by the Observable itself, we call it a cold Observable. When the data is produced outside the Observable, we call it a hot Observable.

Que.q: Q77 : What are custom elements?
Que.a: Custom elements (or Web Components) are a Web Platform feature which extends HTML by allowing you to define a tag whose content is created and controlled by JavaScript code. The browser maintains a CustomElementRegistry of defined custom elements, which maps an instantiable JavaScript class to an HTML tag. Currently this feature is supported by Chrome, Firefox, Opera, and Safari, and available in other browsers through polyfills.

Que.q: Q78 : Do I need to bootstrap custom elements?
Que.a: No, custom elements bootstrap (or start) automatically when they are added to the DOM, and are automatically destroyed when removed from the DOM. Once a custom element is added to the DOM for any page, it looks and behaves like any other HTML element, and does not require any special knowledge of Angular.

Que.q: Q80 : How to transfer components to custom elements?
Que.a: Transforming components to custom elements involves two major steps,

list.Build custom element class: Angular provides the createCustomElement() function for converting an Angular component (along with its dependencies) to a custom element. The conversion process implements NgElementConstructor interface, and creates a constructor class which is used to produce a self-bootstrapping instance of Angular component.
list.Register element class with browser: It uses customElements.define() JS function, to register the configured constructor and its associated custom-element tag with the browser's CustomElementRegistry. When the browser encounters the tag for the registered element, it uses the constructor to create a custom-element instance.

Que.q: Q81 : What are the mapping rules between Angular component and custom element?

list.2: The Component outputs are dispatched as HTML Custom Events, with the name of the custom event matching the output name. For example, component @Output() valueChanged = new EventEmitter() converted as custom element with dispatch event as 'valueChanged'.

Que.q: Q83 : What are different types of compilation in Angular?
Que.a: Angular offers two ways to compile your application.

list.1: Just-in-Time (JIT)
list.2: Ahead-of-Time (AOT)

Que.q: Q84 : What is JIT?
Que.a: Just-in-Time (JIT) is a type of compilation that compiles your app in the browser at runtime. JIT compilation is the default when you run the ng build (build only) or ng serve (build and serve locally) CLI commands. i.e, the below commands used for JIT compilation,

Que.simple_text: The simple container with input property would be as below,
Que.code:
ng build
ng serve

Que.q: Q85 : What is AOT?
Que.a: Ahead-of-Time (AOT) is a type of compilation that compiles your app at build time. For AOT compilation, include the --aot option with the ng build or ng serve command as below,

Que.simple_text: The simple container with input property would be as below,
Que.code:
ng build --aot
ng serve --aot

Que.note: Note: The ng build command with the --prod meta-flag (ng build --prod) compiles with AOT by default.

Que.q: Q86 : Why do we need compilation process?
Que.a: The Angular components and templates cannot be understood by the browser directly. Due to that Angular applications require a compilation process before they can run in a browser. For example, In AOT compilation, both Angular HTML and TypeScript code converted into efficient JavaScript code during the build phase before browser runs it.

Que.q: Q87 : What are the advantages with AOT?
Que.a: Below are the list of AOT benefits,

list.Faster rendering: The browser downloads a pre-compiled version of the application. So it can render the application immediately without compiling the app.
list.Fewer asynchronous requests: It inlines external HTML templates and CSS style sheets within the application javascript which eliminates separate ajax requests.
list.Smaller Angular framework download size: Doesn't require downloading the Angular compiler. Hence it dramatically reduces the application payload.
list.Detect template errors earlier: Detects and reports template binding errors during the build step itself.
list.Better security: It compiles HTML templates and components into JavaScript. So there won't be any injection attacks.

Que.q: Q88 : What are the ways to control AOT compilation?
Que.a: You can control your app compilation in two ways,

list.1: By providing template compiler options in the tsconfig.json file
list.2: By configuring Angular metadata with decorators

Que.q: Q89 : What are the restrictions of metadata?
Que.a: In Angular, You must write metadata with the following general constraints,

list.1: Write expression syntax with in the supported range of javascript features.
list.2: The compiler can only reference symbols which are exported.
list.3: Only call the functions supported by the compiler.
list.4: Decorated and data-bound class members must be public.

Que.q: Q90 : What are the three phases of AOT?
Que.a: The AOT compiler works in three phases,

list.Code Analysis: The compiler records a representation of the source
list.Code generation: It handles the interpretation as well as places restrictions on what it interprets.
list.Validation: In this phase, the Angular template compiler uses the TypeScript compiler to validate the binding expressions in templates.

Que.q: Q100 : What is a service worker and its role in Angular?
Que.a: A service worker is a script that runs in the web browser and manages caching for an application. Starting from 5.0.0 version, Angular ships with a service worker implementation. Angular service worker is designed to optimize the end user experience of using an application over a slow or unreliable network connection, while also minimizing the risks of serving outdated content.

Que.q: Q101 : What are the design goals of service workers?
Que.a: Below are the list of design goals of Angular's service workers,

list.1: It caches an application just like installing a native application
list.2: A running application continues to run with the same version of all files without any incompatible files
list.3: When you refresh the application, it loads the latest fully cached version
list.4: When changes are published then it immediately updates in the background.
list.5: Service workers saves the bandwidth by downloading the resources only when they changed
